mainTopic: What counts as פירכוס (a sign of life) during שחיטה, and when in the שחיטה it must happen
overview: The amud begins by finishing a list: lowing, passing excrement, or wiggling an ear during שחיטה counts as פירכוס, a sign the animal was alive. שמואל gives a broader test: any movement a dying animal does not naturally make counts. So bending a straight leg counts, but straightening a bent one does not. A ברייתא seems to say lowing and excrement do not count. The גמרא answers that only a strong sound or forceful excrement counts, while a weak sound or a trickle does not. Then comes an argument about timing. רב חסדא says the פירכוס must be at the 'end' of שחיטה, which he explains includes the middle. רבא rejects his proof. רב נחמן בר יצחק says even a movement at the beginning counts, and proves it from blood spurting onto the walls of the neck. After a back-and-forth over whether spurting is a stronger or weaker sign, the proof stands. Finally רבא holds that the פירכוס must be at the actual end of שחיטה, and he begins a proof from a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Lowing, excrement, or a wiggling ear count as convulsion
steps.stepSummary: The end of a list of signs: if the animal lows, passes excrement, or wiggles its ear during the שחיטה, that counts as פירכוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the animal lows, passes excrement, or wiggles its ear, that counts as a convulsion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes stating a rule that started just before this section. Certain small actions of the animal during the שחיטה count as פירכוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פירכוס shows the animal was still alive when it was slaughtered, which is needed for the שחיטה to be valid. This list says that even non-limb actions, like a sound, passing excrement, or an ear movement, count as that sign. The ear movement is what שמואל will react to next.

keyTerms.meaning: A convulsion or movement of the animal at slaughter that shows it was alive
Lows (makes a cow-like sound)
Excrement
Wiggled or shook

phrases.english: If it lows, or passed excrement,
or wiggled its ear,
that counts as a convulsion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lowing, passing excrement, or wiggling the ear during slaughter counts as פירכוס.

steps.title: שמואל: any movement a dying animal doesn't make is enough
steps.stepSummary: שמואל asks whether רב ('אבא') really needs something as strong as an ear movement. He states his own broader rule: any movement that is not what a dying animal naturally does counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to them: Does אבא really need the animal to move its ears? I say that any movement which is not something a dying animal does on its own counts as a convulsion.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל reacts to the list by questioning whether such strong signs are needed. He then gives a simpler, broader rule of his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ear movement takes real life force, so requiring it sets a high bar. שמואל says the real test is different. If the movement is something a dying body does anyway, it proves nothing. If it is not, it shows life. This rule could include much smaller movements than an ear wiggle.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it necessary? (here said with surprise, as a challenge)
To move the ears
Things a dying animal does on its own as it dies

steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's rule, 'not what a dying animal does', becomes the test for all the following steps.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Is it necessary, according to אבא,
phrases.notes: 'אבא' is רב's name. שמואל is questioning רב's opinion.

phrases.english: for it to move its ears?
For I say:
any movement that is not
among the things a dying animal does, counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the high bar in step 1 and replaces it with a broader test
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any movement that a dying animal does not naturally make counts as פירכוס.

steps.title: What does a dying animal do?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly counts as 'things a dying animal does'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the things that a dying animal does?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of שמואל's key phrase. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule only works if we know which movements are natural to a dying body. Without that, we cannot tell which movements show life.

keyTerms.meaning: What are they?

phrases.english: What are
the things that a dying animal does?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the key phrase in step 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete definition of 'things a dying animal does'.

steps.title: Straightening a leg is death; bending a straight leg is life
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן reports שמואל's own explanation. Straightening a bent foreleg is what a dying animal does. Bending a straight foreleg is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן said: שמואל himself explained it to me. If the foreleg was bent and the animal straightened it, that is something a dying animal does. If it was straight and the animal bent it, that is something a dying animal does not do.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן answers the question with a clear example he heard directly from שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As an animal dies, its limbs naturally stretch out, so straightening proves nothing. Bending a straight leg takes active effort, so it shows the animal was alive and the שחיטה is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me personally
Bent
Straight, stretched out
Its foreleg (literally, 'its hand')

steps.whatToRemember: Bent leg becoming straight = what a dying animal does, so it is not a sign of life. Straight leg becoming bent = not what a dying animal does, so it is a valid פירכוס.

phrases.english: Rav Anan said:
To me it was explained
by Master Shmuel himself:
if its foreleg was bent and it straightened it,
that is a thing a dying animal does;
if it was straight and it bent it,
that is among the things a dying animal does not do.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עָנָן: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Straightening a bent leg is what a dying animal does. Bending a straight leg is not, so it counts as פירכוס.

steps.title: Isn't this already taught in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל adds. The משנה already says an animal that stretched its leg and did not pull it back is invalid, which implies pulling it back makes it valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned: a small animal that stretched out its foreleg and did not pull it back is invalid, because that is just the soul leaving. That implies that if it pulled it back, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's teaching as unnecessary. It points out that the משנה seems to say the same thing already.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats stretching alone as the natural process of dying. From that, the גמרא infers that bending the leg back shows life. If the משנה already teaches this, the גמרא asks why שמואל had to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asking what is new here)
A small animal (sheep or goat)
The soul leaving the body, the natural process of dying
But this implies (introduces an inference from the wording)

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned:
a small animal that stretched out its foreleg
and did not pull it back is invalid,
because that is nothing but the soul leaving;
this implies that if it pulled it back, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 4 as already taught by the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's teaching, as explained by רב ענן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already implies that bending the leg back shows life, so שמואל's statement seems to add nothing new.

steps.title: שמואל teaches that bending a straight leg alone is enough
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה alone we would have thought the full motion was needed: bent, then straightened, then bent again. שמואל teaches that just bending a leg that was already straight is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had the משנה, I would have said it only counts when the leg was bent, then straightened, and then bent again. But if it was straight and simply bent, it would not count. So שמואל teaches us that it does count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing what שמואל adds beyond the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case begins with a bent leg that stretches and then returns. So we might have thought only that full cycle proves life. שמואל teaches that a leg that started straight and bent counts by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (the mistaken first assumption)
Specifically, only
And then bent it again

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה covers bent, then straightened, then bent again. שמואל adds that a straight leg that simply bends also counts as a valid פירכוס.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. Bending the leg is the sign of life. Straightening it alone is just what happens as the animal dies.

phrases.english: If only from the Mishnah, I would have said:
only where it was bent and it straightened it
and then bent it again,
but if it was straight and it bent it, no;
so he teaches us that it does count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the teaching adds something new beyond the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the full motion (bent, then straightened, then bent again) counts as פירכוס.
steps.terutzMaskana: A straight leg that simply bends is also a valid פירכוס.

steps.title: A ברייתא says lowing and excrement are not signs of life
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that lowing, passing excrement, and wagging the tail during שחיטה are not פירכוס. This contradicts the earlier view on the דף, attributed to רב, that lowing and excrement do count.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: רבי יוסי says that רבי מאיר used to say: if the animal lows during שחיטה, that is not פירכוס. רבי אלעזר son of רבי יוסי says in his name: even if it passed excrement and wagged its tail, that is not פירכוס. So lowing contradicts lowing, and excrement contradicts excrement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that says lowing and excrement do NOT count as signs of life. It then points out that this clashes with the earlier view that they DO count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the דף, lowing and passing excrement were listed as valid פירכוס. The ברייתא says the very same actions are not פירכוס. The גמרא names two separate clashes: one about lowing and one about excrement.

keyTerms.meaning: A convulsion or movement during שחיטה that shows the animal was still alive
Lows, makes a cow-like sound
Excrement
Wagged its tail
It is difficult; there is a contradiction

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: Rabbi Meir would say:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹעָה בִּשְׁעַת שְׁחִיטָה – אֵין זֶה פִּירְכּוּס.
phrases.english: If it lows during slaughter, that is not a convulsion.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשְּׁמוֹ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei says in his name:
Even if it passed excrement and wagged its tail,
that is not a convulsion.
Lowing contradicts lowing,
phrases.notes: Literally 'lowing against lowing': this ברייתא against the earlier view on the דף that lowing does count.

phrases.english: excrement contradicts excrement!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the leg-movement discussion to a ברייתא that challenges the earlier list of valid signs of life.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier view on the דף that lowing and passing excrement count as פירכוס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly says these same actions are not פירכוס, so the two rulings clash.

steps.title: Strong sound versus weak sound, forceful versus trickling
steps.stepSummary: Both clashes are resolved by splitting the cases. A strong sound counts and a muffled one does not. Excrement pushed out with force counts, but a trickle does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lowing against lowing is not a problem: this one is when its voice is strong, that one is when its voice is weak. Excrement against excrement is also not a problem: here it is trickling out, there it is shooting out with force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers each contradiction by showing the two sources are talking about different kinds of lowing and different kinds of excrement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A strong, full sound or forceful excrement takes real effort, so it shows life and counts as פירכוס. A weak sound or a trickle can happen to a dying animal on its own, so the ברייתא says it does not count. Both sources are right, each about its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: Its voice is thick and strong
Its voice is dim and weak
Trickling out slowly
Shooting out with force

steps.whatToRemember: Lowing and excrement count as פירכוס only when they are strong and forceful. A weak sound or a trickle does not count.

phrases.english: Lowing against lowing is not difficult:
this is where its voice is strong,
phrases.notes: This is the view that lowing counts.

phrases.english: that is where its voice is weak.
Excrement against excrement is also not difficult:
here, when it trickles out,
phrases.notes: Careful, the order flips: this first case is the ברייתא, which says it does not count.

phrases.english: there, when it shoots out with force.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both contradictions raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source refers to a different version of the action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lowing and excrement are either always פירכוס or never פירכוס.
steps.terutzMaskana: Strong lowing and forceful excrement count. Weak lowing and trickling excrement do not.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the פירכוס must be at the end of שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא states that the פירכוס the חכמים spoke about must happen at the end of the שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: the פירכוס that the חכמים spoke about is at the end of שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a new rule about WHEN the sign of life has to happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about WHAT movements count. רב חסדא adds a timing rule. The wording 'end of שחיטה' will be clarified in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: That they (the חכמים) said
The end of the slaughter

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The convulsion they spoke of is at the end of slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the timing of the פירכוס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A valid פירכוס is one that happens at the end of the שחיטה.

steps.title: What does 'end of שחיטה' mean
steps.stepSummary: The question is asked: what exactly is meant by 'at the end of שחיטה'?
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'at the end of שחיטה' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: A short question that sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase could mean only after the cut is finished, or something broader. The question asks for the exact meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of

phrases.english: What is 'at the end of slaughter'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to clarify the wording of רב חסדא's rule in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact time span meant by 'end of שחיטה'.

steps.title: It means even in the middle, just not the very start
steps.stepSummary: 'End of שחיטה' really includes the middle of the שחיטה. It only comes to rule out movements at the very beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means in the middle of שחיטה. It comes to exclude the beginning of שחיטה, which does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer explains that 'end' is a loose word here. A movement in the middle of the שחיטה counts too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only time ruled out is the very start of the cut. From the middle onward, a movement counts as a sign of life.

keyTerms.meaning: The middle of the slaughter
To exclude, to rule out
The beginning of the slaughter

steps.confusionAlert: Do not take 'end of שחיטה' literally. It includes the middle. Only the very beginning is excluded.

phrases.english: In the middle of slaughter,
to exclude the beginning of slaughter, which does not count.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאֶמְצַע שְׁחִיטָה, לְאַפּוֹקֵי תְּחִלַּת שְׁחִיטָה דְּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'End' includes the middle of the שחיטה. Only the very start is excluded.

steps.title: רב חסדא's proof from the משנה about the stretched leg
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא proves his point from the משנה: a small animal that stretched its leg and did not pull it back is invalid. That case cannot be at the very end, since we would not require the animal to live on after the שחיטה. So it must be in the middle, which shows a movement in the middle counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: where do I learn this from? From the משנה: a small animal that stretched out its foreleg and did not pull it back is invalid. When did this happen? If you say at the end of the שחיטה, must the animal keep living that long afterward? Rather, isn't it talking about the middle of the שחיטה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא brings a proof from the משנה that a movement in the middle of the שחיטה counts as a sign of life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה implies that pulling the leg back makes the animal valid. If that meant pulling it back after the cut is finished, the animal would have to keep living after the שחיטה, which is too much to expect. So the משנה must mean pulling it back during the שחיטה, and that counts.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (a request for a source)
A small animal, like a sheep or goat
Pulled it back
If you say
Keep living on and on
Rather, is it not that

steps.whatToRemember: A movement in the middle of the שחיטה counts as פירכוס. Only a movement at the very start does not. The proof is the משנה about the leg that was stretched and not pulled back.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: From where do I say it?
As we learned in the Mishnah:
A small animal that stretched out its foreleg
and did not pull it back is invalid.
When?
If you say at the end of slaughter,
must it go on living that long?
phrases.notes: He means: we can't expect the animal to stay alive after the cut is done just to pull its leg back.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it in the middle of slaughter?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source from the משנה for the explanation given in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That a פירכוס in the middle of the שחיטה counts
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: a small animal that stretched its foreleg and did not pull it back is invalid, which implies that pulling it back makes it valid

steps.title: רבא pushes away רב חסדא's proof
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the case in the משנה can be at the very end of the שחיטה, because an animal that cannot pull its leg back at the end was already dead before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Really, the case is at the end of the שחיטה. I say that any animal that does not pull its leg back at the end of the שחיטה surely lost its life before that.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב חסדא's proof from step 12. He shows that the case in the משנה can still be at the very end of the שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא argued that the משנה cannot be about the end, since we do not demand that the animal live on after the cut. רבא says the point is different: pulling the leg back is a sign of life, and an animal too weak to do it at the end was already dead earlier. So the משנה proves nothing about movements in the middle.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth. Used to keep the first reading and reject the other side's proof.
It is clearly known
Its life (soul) was taken away

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Really, it is at the end of the slaughter,
for I say:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינָהּ עוֹשֶׂה כֵּן בְּסוֹף שְׁחִיטָה –
phrases.english: any animal that does not do so at the end of the slaughter,
phrases.notes: "Do so" means pull back the leg it stretched out, from the משנה case in step 12.

phrases.aramaic: בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁנִּשְׁמָתָהּ נְטוּלָה הֵימֶנָּה קוֹדֶם לָכֵן.
phrases.english: it is known that its life was taken from it before that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: לְעוֹלָם בְּסוֹף שְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only רב חסדא's proof from the משנה. It does not reject the idea that a movement in the middle might count.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read as being about the very end: failing to pull the leg back at the end shows the animal was already dead.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: even a movement at the start counts
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the פירכוס the חכמים spoke about counts even at the beginning of the שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The movement the חכמים spoke about counts even at the beginning of the שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives a different view. He holds that a movement at the very beginning of the שחיטה is also a good sign of life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא ruled out movements at the beginning (step 11). רב נחמן בר יצחק goes further and allows even those. So now we have a clear argument about the timing of the sign of life.

keyTerms.meaning: The jerking movement of a slaughtered animal that shows it was alive
The beginning of the slaughtering cut

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
The convulsion that they spoke of,
is even at the beginning of the slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: פִּירְכּוּס שֶׁאָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a view opposed to רב חסדא's and רבא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פירכוס even at the beginning of the שחיטה shows the animal was alive.

steps.title: Proof from blood on the walls of the neck
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק proves his view from רבי שמעון's case of blood found on the walls. שמואל says these are the walls of the neck. If only a sign at the end counts, we should worry the blood spurted at the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: How do I know this? From the משנה. רבי שמעון said: If someone slaughters at night and the next morning finds the walls full of blood, the animal is כשרה, because the blood spurted. This follows רבי אליעזר's view. שמואל said: The walls meant are the walls of the neck where the cut was made. If a sign at the beginning counts, this works well. But if only a sign at the end counts, we should worry that the blood spurted at the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק backs up his view with a source. He shows that רבי שמעון's ruling only makes sense if a sign at the beginning of the שחיטה counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood on the walls of the neck could have spurted at any point in the cut, even at the very start. רבי שמעון still calls the animal כשרה without asking when it happened. That fits only if a sign of life at the beginning is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (I will now bring my proof)
It spurted (the blood shot out with force)
The walls of the place of the cut, meaning the sides of the neck
It works out fine if
Let us worry about

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
From where do I say it?
As we learned: Rabbi Shimon said:
One who slaughters at night,
and the next day found walls full of blood,
it is valid, because it spurted,
and this follows the measure of Rabbi Eliezer.
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר holds that spurting blood is enough to show the animal was alive.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
We learned about the walls of the place of slaughter.
phrases.notes: He means the sides of the neck around the cut, not the walls of the house.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא בִּתְחִלַּת שְׁחִיטָה – שַׁפִּיר,
phrases.english: Granted, if you say a sign at the beginning of the slaughter counts, it works well,
but if you say only at the end of the slaughter,
let us worry that perhaps it spurted at the beginning of the slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the ruling in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That a sign of life at the beginning of the שחיטה counts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון in the משנה (blood on the walls), as explained by שמואל (the walls of the neck).

steps.title: Spurting blood may be a stronger sign
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Spurting blood may be a stronger sign than a leg movement, so it can count even at the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps spurting is different, because it is a stronger sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof from step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that spurting and leg movements follow the same timing rule. The גמרא says spurting may be a stronger sign of life, so it can work even at the start. A leg movement could still need to be at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
It is different
Stronger, better

steps.confusionAlert: This does not prove that רב נחמן בר יצחק is wrong. It only shows that his proof is not strong enough.

phrases.english: But perhaps spurting is different,
since it is stronger.
phrases.notes: He means spurting is a stronger sign of life than stretching or bending a leg.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from spurting blood, not רב נחמן בר יצחק's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof treats spurting like a leg movement. Spurting may be a stronger sign, so its timing rule may be different.

steps.title: How can spurting be stronger, if רבי אליעזר calls it 'enough'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea from Step 16 that spurting blood is a stronger sign of life than a leg movement. It quotes רבי אליעזר in the משנה, who says spurting is "enough," which sounds like a lenient, weaker sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is spurting really stronger? But we learned in the משנה that רבי אליעזר says: it is enough if the blood spurted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the rejection it just made in Step 16. It asks how spurting can be a strong sign when רבי אליעזר's wording makes it sound like the easy option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "דַּיָּיהּ" ("it is enough") is used for a lenient minimum. That shows רבי אליעזר is asking for less than the other opinions, so spurting looks like a weaker sign. If so, Step 16's claim that spurting is stronger than a leg movement seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Better or stronger; here, a stronger sign that the animal was alive
It is enough for it; a lenient, minimum requirement
It spurted (the blood shot out from the neck)

phrases.english: And is it really stronger? But didn't we learn in the Mishnah:
phrases.notes: "It" is spurting blood. Step 16 claimed it might be a stronger sign than a leg movement.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
It is enough if the blood spurted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning behind the rejection in Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 16's claim that spurting blood is a stronger sign than a leg movement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's word "enough" shows spurting is a lenient, weaker requirement, not a stronger one.

steps.title: Spurting is in the middle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that spurting is weaker than רבן גמליאל's requirement but stronger than the חכמים's requirement. So it can still be stronger than a single leg movement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Spurting is weaker than what רבן גמליאל requires, but stronger than what the חכמים require.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by placing spurting in the middle of the three opinions in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's "enough" is lenient only compared to רבן גמליאל, who asks for a lot. Compared to the חכמים, who are satisfied with one limb moving, spurting is the stronger sign. So Step 16's rejection still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Light; here, a weaker or easier sign
The Sages, the majority opinion in the משנה (also called חכמים)

phrases.english: It is weaker than Rabban Gamliel's sign,
phrases.notes: רבן גמליאל asks for more: movement of both the front leg and the back leg.

phrases.english: but stronger than the Rabbis' sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ranking the opinions: spurting sits between the two other views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי אליעזר says "enough," spurting is the weakest sign of all
steps.terutzMaskana: Spurting is weaker only compared to רבן גמליאל, but stronger than the חכמים' single limb movement

steps.title: Is spurting really stronger than the חכמים' sign?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reports a challenge he heard in the name of the father of בר אבוברם, or his brother. How can spurting be stronger than the חכמים' sign, when the חכמים say the animal is valid only "עד" ("when") it moves its front leg or back leg?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: סמא בר חילקאי told me that the father of בר אבוברם, and some say the brother of בר אבוברם, asked: Is spurting really stronger than the חכמים' sign? But we learned in the משנה: the חכמים say, only when it moves its front leg or its back leg.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge attacks the answer from Step 18. The challenger questions whether spurting is really stronger than the חכמים' sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge rests on the word "עד" ("only when") in the חכמים' statement. That word sounds like they are being stricter, asking for more than someone else. The next two steps explain exactly why this matters.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a difficulty about it
Only when it moves (twitches) a limb
A twitch or movement of a limb that shows the animal was alive

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבִינָא: אָמַר לִי סַמָּא בַּר חִילְקַאי,
phrases.english: Ravina said: Samma bar Ḥilkai told me,
the father of bar Abuveram raised a difficulty about it,
and some say it was the brother of bar Abuveram:
Is spurting really stronger than the Rabbis' sign?
But didn't we learn in the Mishnah: And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁתְּפַרְכֵּס אוֹ בַיָּד אוֹ בָרֶגֶל.
phrases.english: Only when it moves either its front leg or its back leg.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 18's claim that spurting is stronger than the חכמים' sign
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים use the word "עד," which sounds like they are being stricter than another opinion. That would make spurting weaker than their sign.

steps.title: Who are the חכמים answering? Not רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains the challenge. He asks which opinion the חכמים are responding to. It cannot be רבן גמליאל, because then they would be more lenient and should have said "כיון" ("once"), not "עד" ("only when").
steps.simpleTranslation: Which opinion are the חכמים responding to? If you say רבן גמליאל, they should have said "once it moved."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is laying out the logic behind the challenge. Here it rules out one possibility, and that sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Compared to רבן גמליאל, who wants both legs to move, the חכמים are more lenient. A lenient reply would say "once it moved one limb, that is enough." Since they said "עד," a strict word, they are not replying to רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: On which opinion are they standing? Which view are they responding to?
If you say; offering a possibility in order to test it
Once, as soon as; wording that makes something easier
It should have said

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the two words. "עד" ("only when") is strict wording: you need at least this much. "כיון" ("once") is lenient wording: this much is already enough. The whole challenge turns on which word the חכמים used.

phrases.english: To which opinion are the Rabbis responding?
If you say they are responding to Rabban Gamliel,
they should have said "once it moved"!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן אַהֵי קָיְימִי? אִילֵּימָא אַדְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the challenge in Step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion in the משנה the חכמים are responding to
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not רבן גמליאל, because a reply to him would use the lenient word "כיון"

steps.title: They are answering רבי אליעזר, so spurting must be weaker
steps.stepSummary: So the חכמים must be responding to רבי אליעזר. If spurting were stronger than their sign, why would they say "עד," as if they were asking for more? This shows spurting is weaker than a limb movement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious they are responding to רבי אליעזר. And if spurting is stronger, what is the meaning of "only when"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge. The חכמים are replying to רבי אליעזר in a strict way, so spurting must be the weaker sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the חכמים reply to רבי אליעזר with "עד," they are saying spurting alone is not enough and a limb movement is needed. That makes spurting weaker than a limb movement, which goes against Step 18. It also knocks out Step 16's rejection, so רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof from Step 15 is back: if a weaker sign counts at the beginning, a leg movement surely does.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; leaving the first possibility for another one
It is obvious
What is the point of the word "until / only when"?

steps.whatToRemember: Because the חכמים reply to רבי אליעזר with "עד," spurting blood is a weaker sign than a limb movement. So Step 16's rejection falls, and רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof that a movement at the beginning of the שחיטה counts stands again.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step decides whether רב נחמן בר יצחק's view, that a פירכוס at the beginning of the שחיטה is valid, has support from the משנה.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious they are responding to Rabbi Eliezer,
and if spurting is stronger, what is the point of saying "only when"?
phrases.notes: If spurting were stronger, the חכמים would be the lenient ones, and they should have said "כיון," not "עד."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא אַדְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וְאִי עֲדִיף, מַאי עַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning begun in Step 20 and finishes the challenge of Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 18's answer, and with it Step 16's rejection of רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים reply to רבי אליעזר with the strict word "עד," so spurting is weaker than a limb movement. If even the weaker sign counts at the beginning, a leg movement at the beginning surely counts.

steps.title: רבא: the convulsion must come at the end of the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the פירכוס the חכמים spoke about counts only if it happens at the end of the שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פירכוס that the חכמים spoke about is one that happens at the end of the שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own view in the argument about timing. He says the convulsion that proves the animal was alive must happen at the end of the שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The timing question has been debated since step 9: רב חסדא said 'end' includes the middle, and רב נחמן בר יצחק said even the beginning counts. רבא now gives his own view in this dispute. It fits what he told רב חסדא in step 13, where he read the משנה as being about the actual end of the שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: A convulsion or jerking movement of the animal, used as a sign that it was still alive
Kosher slaughter, cutting the animal's throat in the proper way
At the end of the slaughter
That they (the חכמים) said; points back to the rule in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: רבא's 'end of שחיטה' is not the same as רב חסדא's. רב חסדא read 'end' loosely to include the middle. רבא means the actual end, as he argued in step 13.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the time a person must check for the sign of life. A movement at the wrong time would not prove the animal was alive at שחיטה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The convulsion that they said
phrases.notes: "They" means the חכמים, who said a convulsion shows the animal was alive.

phrases.english: is at the end of the slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third view in the timing argument: unlike רב חסדא (middle counts) and רב נחמן בר יצחק (beginning counts), רבא requires the actual end, matching his reply in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The convulsion that counts as a sign of life must happen at the end of the שחיטה.

steps.title: רבא begins his proof from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks where he learns his rule from and starts quoting a ברייתא on the פסוק that begins with the word "שור".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From where do I say this? As it is taught in a ברייתא: "A bull..."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is getting ready to prove his rule. He asks for his own source and starts quoting a ברייתא, but the quote continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking "מנא אמינא לה" is how a sage opens his own proof. The ברייתא is about the פסוק "שור או כשב או עז כי יולד". How it proves the timing of the convulsion will only become clear when the quote continues.

keyTerms.meaning: "From where do I say it?" A sage asks for his own source and then brings a proof
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה, introduced here by דתניא
Bull or ox; the first word of the פסוק being quoted

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say it?
phrases.notes: He is about to bring a source for his own rule from Step 22.

phrases.english: As it is taught: "A bull
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:27. The quote keeps going in the next part of the text.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא starts to support his own rule from Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that the convulsion must happen at the end of the שחיטה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on the פסוק "שור או כשב או עז כי יולד" (ויקרא 22:27); the full quote continues in the next part of the text
